performance.threshold: Reopenings in a row with no human answer between them: at most one more than the recorded material answers. The report the latest answer was given on is reopened as soon as it loses one; each later reopening must carry an answer no report written since that answer, that one included, carried. Adopting the mandate or failing G0 adds none.
performance.measured: test/v2/specification-reopening.test.ts at 07f4c38, under Node 24.21.0. 6c: reports that take one answer back and lose the other in turn stop being reopened at the first one that carries only answers already carried; 6b: a reopened report that gains nothing is not reopened; 6g: a human adoption of the mandate does not reopen the adopted report, which goes to G1; 6h and 6j: what the report the latest answer was given on carries, itself or by inheritance, counts as already carried. 6b and 6c fail on the code before the story (bdebd23), 6g on 5364797; 6h and 6j fail under the mutations recorded in specs/verifications/e01s01-cycle-rouge-vert.md.
performance.note: Each reopening is one specify intervention; the bound is what limits their cost (threat M7). No campaign measures it with a real model: the real campaign belongs to e01s05.

reliability.measured: 6a: the reopened report that renames the requirement Q1 was bound to and asks nothing is reopened, the request names the answer to declare, and the change passes G1. 6f and 6i: the report an answer was given on is written again as soon as it ignores one, even when it is not the first report. On the real report 183 of java-flashnext-L2 (dia_mu8m4cqjce00c7bf75), the built kernel returns ignored [Q1], reopen true at 8a7c8dd and again at 07f4c38; the kernel before the story returns ignored [], settled true, which is how that change was lost at G1.
